Recent image-to-image translation work has been influenced by the cycleGAN design, using adaptive instance normalization layers. This design has been a key factor in the success of such applications, largely due to its simplicity and efficiency. However, the underlying assumption of having well-organized domain labels for training adaptive IN layers is a significant limitation. In response to this constraint, we introduce a new layer called SortIN, which sorts the feature maps of a given input before applying normalization. By doing so, we are able to eliminate the reliance on adaptive IN layers while achieving cycle stability. Additionally, our proposed method offers several benefits, including a substantial reduction in computational requirements and the ability to facilitate directionality of data sorting. We validate the effectiveness of SortIN by integrating it into a cycleGAN design and utilizing it as a baseline for comparisons with existing AdaIN-based methods. Our findings indicate that SortIN performs on par with AdaIN-based cycleGAN designs in various image-to-image translation tasks while exhibiting superior performance in scenarios with limited training data.

We introduce a novel multi-view score function and an associated ordered batch rearrangement strategy for paired dataset augmentation. This method enhances the diversity of data used for predicting each view. As a result, a novel end-to-end dialog understanding model is proposed, leveraging the multi-view score function to increase diversity during controlled data augmentation. In this model, each view is trained simultaneously, sharing the same dialog representation. Our experiments demonstrate that this method surpasses multiple strong baselines in dialog state tracking and intention recognition tasks.

This paper derives the conformal $\eta$-Ricci-Yamabe soliton equation in an arbitrary dimension and a specific potential vector field, establishing a connection between the soliton and the Laplace equation. Subsequently, the soliton equation is reduced to a quadratic differential equation in the potential vector field, which is then expressed in terms of a potential function, resulting in the Laplace equation with the soliton and the Laplace equation itself as specific cases.

In this study, we examine the complex structure of halos by combining deformed shape and rotational state principles. Our analysis indicates that high-spin rotational states within halos possess distinct, offset prolate and oblate rotational configurations, which convert into one another as spin increases. This phenomenon results in alternating prolate and oblate density distributions in halos. Additionally, our research reveals that merging these rotational states can produce unique, multi-horn structures within halos. To further investigate these findings, we developed a new parametric shape description, allowing for in-depth analysis of the merging of rotational states and resulting shape transformations. Our results provide theoretical support for recently observed multi-horn structures in exotic nuclei.

This paper introduces BasicVSR++, a highly efficient video restoration model, 
building on the foundations laid by BasicVSR. By fine-tuning the model's learnable 
deblocking filter and spatial detail processor components, BasicVSR++ demonstrates 
substantial improvements, achieving a 13.1% average better PSNR performance and 
double the efficiency in video restoration tasks. Our work showcases the efficacy 
of learning-based processing components and highlights the potential for precise 
video processing. Additionally, our efficient design paves the way for various 
video processing applications.

In this research, we have derived universal modifications to parton distribution functions of W and Z bosons, valid for all energies. These modifications are specifically focused on addressing limitations in current PDF fits, which fail to account for the precise behavior of boson PDFs in high-energy situations, even in areas where experimental data is readily available. As a result, our proposed changes can enhance the accuracy of theoretical predictions for deep-inelastic scattering, Higgs boson production, and vector boson scattering in the high-energy range. We have incorporated these modifications into a set of initial conditions for the evolution of boson PDFs and demonstrated their impact within the context of the MMRT resummation framework for DIS, Higgs production in deep-inelastic scattering and Higgs production in vector boson scattering at high energies.

In multi-task reinforcement learning, using a single dynamics model that accounts for various task dynamics can have unintended consequences, such as the learned model focusing on contrasting the current task from all other tasks. To address this issue, we propose using a dynamics model that is constrained to resemble a specific task's dynamics and can be learned through contrastive loss during the reinforcement learning process. This approach allows us to develop a suitable dynamics model for each individual task and significantly improves the performance in scenarios involving multiple tasks.

This study explores how boundary components affect the composition of solutions to differential equations on noncompact, multidimensional manifolds. We establish criteria for determining whether a given differential equation permits a diverse range of solutions on such manifolds, despite restrictions imposed by compact boundary areas. Additionally, we develop methods for identifying specific patterns of solution composition and proving the existence of particular solution types. These advances build upon previous research, expanding our understanding of the relationship between boundary components and solution composition across complex geometric settings.

In 1936, Godel discovered a famous incompleteness theorem, which demonstrates that any robust formal mathematical system has inherently incomplete axioms. However, these theorems only apply to a specific subset of formulas - those expressing the existence of a proof within the formal system. Rosser built upon this idea by creating a modified version of Godel's second incompleteness theorem specific to formal systems that are consistent. His innovation allowed the application of the theorems to a broader set of formulas. In our research, we extend Rosser's concept to a variety of formal systems, including Peano Arithmetic and the lambda-calculus, using a concept called self-proofability. We also explore connections between our findings and both Godel's incompleteness theorems and the Diagonalization theorem.

Hadama's three circles theorem, extending to R^n, links monogenic functions to a specific area formula. This connection forms the basis for a new approach to calculating the area of a given plane region, even those that are highly complex, via monogenic functions. A key aspect of this method is determining a well-defined, specific monogenic function for each given area. In this paper, we explore ways to accomplish this by examining various strategies to identify suitable parameters for both the rotation and scaling components of Hadama's formula. This investigation includes a look at how the area of a given region can be approximated through the use of partial derivatives of a particular potential function. Additionally, this paper delves into the relationship between such a potential function and a type of harmonic mapping, also exploring how this connection can be applied to solve inverse problems related to Hadama's three circles theorem.

The process of choosing a balanced sample is critical in statistical research, yet it's often hindered by conventional methodology's limitations. A new algorithm, inspired by the loopy binary partitioning approach, has been developed to address this challenge. This algorithm efficiently identifies a balanced subset within large datasets by leveraging parallel processing capabilities. Through experimentation with synthetic and real-world datasets, the algorithm's effectiveness was demonstrated, showcasing its ability to yield high-quality results even in data scenarios with significant dimensions.

Following the success of direct regression in camera calibration, we explored a straightforward approach that directly predicts the relative pose and projection parameters between a robot's end effector and a target object using a single RGBD image. We demonstrated the feasibility of this method using a large-scale dataset recently proposed for target localization tasks. Compared to traditional approaches, our experiments revealed that direct regression yields comparable results with minimal training data, outperforming classical methods when trained on a larger dataset. Additionally, our analysis showed that directly regressing on the projection parameters produces more accurate results than optimizing classical methods. However, we also observed that classical methods with extensive training data can match the performance of direct regression. To further improve direct regression, we proposed a modified version that utilizes both end effector maps and target maps as inputs, resulting in significant improvements.

This paper delves into the advantages of a specific reformulated conditional
Wasserstein GAN, namely the regularized conditional Wasserstein GAN, when utilizing
posterior samples for imaging tasks. We demonstrate that it yields a viable method
for obtaining additional information in medical imaging. We also explore a data
efficiency enhancement based on the reformulated generator network. We evaluate the
performance of this efficient generator on two imaging applications: an experimental
study involving single-ray data and a CT reconstruction scenario. Our study shows
that the reformulated generator is capable of extracting useful posterior information
even with limited training data. Furthermore, the proposed enhancement yields a
significant reduction in training time.

This paper explores the concept of almost invariant subspaces in fractional linear systems and highlights the limitations of the standard Weyl calculus to capture this property. We define a modified Weyl calculus and establish the required properties for this new calculus. Additionally, this study demonstrates the feasibility of almost invariant subspaces in fractional linear systems under specific technical conditions and examines the relationship between this ability and the spectrum of the operator.

In this study, we investigate the efficiency of multi-hop THz links that can dynamically adjust their configuration. We developed a dynamic beam training technique that adjusts the beam training period, bandwidth, and data rate to optimize energy per bit. The optimal dynamic parameters are derived to minimize energy per bit, with the constraint that beam training time cannot exceed a maximum. The proposed dynamic technique is compared to traditional methods, demonstrating a significant improvement in energy per bit - up to 120 dB - for both single-hop and multi-hop links, and is compatible with current and near-future standards, including 5G, 6G, and future standards. The findings can guide the design of terahertz communication systems, encouraging standardizers to consider the efficiency of beam training.

We've carried out high-sensitivity radio observations of the well-known binary millisecond pulsar B1133+16, covering 11 years and consisting of 46 sessions. Our data allowed us to identify 23 individual scattering screens surrounding the pulsar, increasing the previous count by nearly 50%. Notably, we found that these screens follow the expected characteristics of scattering around the Earth, with many sharing a common origin and appearance over time. Interestingly, there are also three distinct screens that haven't been previously reported, located at greater distances from Earth. These additional screens particularly reveal signs of relative motion, which can be linked to the Earth's viewpoint. Furthermore, we were able to link two interstellar scintillation patterns to specific screens, and for the first time with a binary millisecond pulsar, we detected interference from the scintillation pattern originating from the screen closest to Earth, which occurs when the Earth passes through the innermost point of its orbit around the pulsar. This phenomenon, which we were able to model and predict, will repeat in the future based on the Earth's orbital period.

Recently, deep learning models that use limited or no spectral information have achieved notable success in speech analysis, particularly with the introduction of quasi-periodic network architectures. These types of models face significant challenges when dealing with periodic inputs, for which the network may become stuck in local minima or fail to achieve optimal performance. To tackle this issue, we propose a cascaded quasi-periodic network that is able to achieve better results on a set of synthetic and real-world data sets. The key advantages of this network include its ability to model multiple frequency scales and learn temporal dependencies through the gradual passing of features between stages. Compared to standard network architectures, the cascaded network shows a range of improvements, including a decrease in the number of required parameters and the ability to achieve better results with a smaller dataset.

Human annotators expend considerable time and resources to manually label and prepare text documents for effective machine learning usage. By equipping annotators with appropriate technology, their productivity can significantly increase, enabling the efficient use of learned models for various natural language processing tasks. This paper introduces an innovative, integrated system called TextPro that provides a comprehensive set of tools to streamline the annotation process for both small-scale and large-scale projects. Key features of TextPro include data formatting, cleanup, and conversion capabilities as well as customized annotation guides that can be designed by team leaders or supervisors to guide annotators through the labeling process. Additionally, TextPro offers a range of annotation tools, data quality assurance checks, and data management functionalities that include a customizable database and reporting features accessible via both a graphical user interface and a Python API. The design and functionality of TextPro have been influenced by industry-standard annotation software, and the system is particularly suited for processing large datasets, incorporating applications of TextPro to datasets spanning 100,000 documents illustrate its scalability and utility.

The upcoming generation of high accuracy instruments aimed at detecting biomarkers in exoplanet atmospheres, particularly the Diableado telescope, will significantly benefit from this study. This research focuses on temperate planets located within their stars' habitable zones and investigates how the metal content in their atmospheres varies with planetary parameters. It's observed that the metal abundance is correlated with the metal content in the host star and the planet's mass, but the abundance of specific gases like CO, CO2, and NH3 depends on the metal content in the atmosphere rather than the planet's mass or orbital period. Ultimately, the study finds that the metal content in these systems is generally average to above average, reflecting the parent stars' characteristics.

We've developed a new Gelfand-Dyatlov-Kenyon wall-crossing formula for the Epsilon-energy level density of a cubic billiard at finite temperatures. This involves introducing a non-Majorana peak within the spectrum and observing how it changes at non-zero temperatures. Specifically, we find that the zero-energy peak induced by non-Majorana effects undergoes a significant transformation - it breaks apart and becomes a more intricate feature within the spectrum. As temperatures continue to rise, we notice that this peak begins to reassemble and eventually resumes its original form at high temperatures, displaying an intriguing heating pattern.

Road inspection is an essential activity that requires checking roads for conditions such as cracks, potholes, and weather-related damage. Maintaining healthy roads necessitates frequent inspections. The process of conducting these inspections can be time-consuming, however, our research offers an efficient solution by developing a groundbreaking platform called RoadAtlas. This pioneering system combines cutting-edge technology, specifically computer vision and machine learning, to create an innovative tool for analyzing road conditions. The key benefits of RoadAtlas are: 

- Streamlined inspection process: 
  By utilizing our cloud-based platform, users can easily upload video footage from road inspections and quickly obtain accurate analyses of road conditions within a matter of minutes.

- Enhanced accuracy: 
  Our automated analysis system, built with TensorFlow and OpenCV, ensures precise detection of defects in roads by leveraging machine learning. This allows for the standardization of inspection results, making data comparison easier. The incorporation of spatial reasoning algorithms into our vision toolkit enhances the capability of our automated analysis system to accurately identify the layout of roads, bridges, and signs. 

  The design of RoadAtlas facilitates seamless collaboration and data sharing among different stakeholders involved in the inspection process, the transportation department. The implementation of our technology through mobile apps and an automated data collection system on a vehicle in testing phases demonstrates its practical feasibility. 

  By providing an open-source framework, RoadAtlas empowers the global community to contribute to the development of this innovative technology, thus offering numerous opportunities for customization and adaptation to meet the unique needs

Extension of topological Hochschild homology calculations of Bergman, Gillam and Polidore to bicategories is demonstrated through the introduction of the notion of shadows in a monoidal bicategorical framework. This leads to a theoretical topological Hochschild homology calculation for any bicategory, with the result being verified to align with the expected outcomes. Additionally, this approach results in a more direct understanding of the topological Hochschild homology of topological K-theory.

We introduce the VGG-Sound Source (VGG-SS) benchmark, a comprehensive source separation dataset consisting of 1200 audio clips, alongside precise source annotations and metrics for objective evaluation. The dataset distinguishes itself from other existing datasets in several key ways: it encompasses a broad range of source types, includes difficult mixtures, and is supported by a range of metrics tailored to source separation tasks. Leveraging the powerful capabilities of the VGG-Sound dataset, we anticipate that VGG-SS will play a significant role in advancing source separation research and attracting more attention from industry professionals in the field.

This paper introduces a novel framework for complex network analysis within the Euclidean space, specifically in the Lorentzian space. We develop the Lorentzian graph convolutional network (LGCN), a model that generalizes existing hyperbolic graph convolutional networks and improves their performance. LGCN demonstrates the ability to extract more accurate and detailed node feature representations from complex networks. We further explore the incorporation of latent nodes into the LGCN framework and provide a practical implementation of LGCN with experimental results and numerical evaluations.

This paper investigates a stability result for an inverse problem involving a nonhomogeneous acoustic equation within the context of an observability inequality. Given limited initial observation data, the goal is to recover both the nonhomogeneous term and the wave operator's observability constant. Our approach utilizes an operator-theoretic argument to establish a continuous dependence statement, resulting in a stability estimate expressed in terms of the best approximation term in a suitable function space.

In a optomechanical system that combines a microdisk optomechanically linked to a microsphere, we demonstrate the principle of Total Internal Reflection Shadow (TSS) and analyze its spectral impact. By employing a finite difference method, we visualize the TSS effect and illustrate that it results from a combination of reflection, absorption, and radiation pressure within the optomechanical system. We also find that TSS occurs over a specific, narrow spectral range near the optomechanical system's anti-Debye wave number, and that it may be controlled through proper choice of optomechanical parameters. Furthermore, we discover that TSS effect amplifies the optomechanical response by increasing the shift in resonant frequency, thus making it possible to observe TSS even in systems where it is not noticeable, as long as the incident light intensity is high enough.

We investigate the presence of atoms in u-calculus without function symbols or relational symbols, also known as solvable u-calculus. Two variants are considered: one permits unbounded negation in u-formulas, while the other is limited to positive occurrences of subgoals. Both variants are studied with and without inequality atoms. The core questions examined are the u-calculus's expressive power, satisfiability, and finite model property. Our findings demonstrate that unbounded negation atoms make the solvable u-calculus expressive but satisfiability can be guaranteed when limited to positive atoms alone. Moreover, both solvable and universal solvable u-calculi possess the finite model property. Additionally, we show that the presence of inequality atoms is equivalent to that of equality atoms.

The Tsallis distribution has a broad application in statistics and is widely used to model non-extensive systems. Although it may seem unrelated at first, the Tsallis distribution can be viewed through the lens of social dynamics, where individuals make independent, yet biased, decisions that align with maximum entropy principles. These decisions then give rise to the Tsallis distribution. In this study, we redefine the Tsallis entropy to incorporate memory effects within the system, leading to a more comprehensive understanding of the Tsallis distribution. We specifically examine how memory exponents evolve over time, revealing a complex, non-linear pattern. To further analyze this phenomenon, we introduce a new concept called the "memory spectrum," which summarizes the system's memory dynamics. The concepts we introduce here have a broad application and can be applied to any system that follows the Tsallis distribution. In fact, we also provide an example by analyzing a famous dataset of income data from Portugal.

We investigate the implications of introducing a mass term in the perturbations of gravitational waves, which results in additional screening phenomena affecting the quasinormal modes of a black hole. In the context of the linearized gravity theory, this mass term causes the degeneracy of the two scalar degrees of freedom to break down, resulting in one massless mode and one massive mode. Our team has previously derived the quasinormal mode frequencies subject to this mass term's constraint. In contrast, we also examine the impact of the mass term on gravitational waves emitted from a system of inspiraling binary stars. Our study considers both the case when gravitational waves are directly detected and the case when they influence the orbital period of binary stars through the de Chanelier effect. The resulting modifications are expressed in terms of the post-Newtonian parameters, which show how the mass term affects these relations.

Building on a conjecture by Choudhury, Ghoshal, and Janssen, we investigate the computational complexity of determining whether extended double covers of signed graphs are efficiently solvable in a planar context. Our analysis confirms the conjecture for a specific class of signed graphs known as layerable signed graphs, while also establishing that the associated decision problem for this class retains NP-complexity even in the presence of a topological constraint. Additionally, we analyze the computational complexity of determining whether an extended double cover of a signed graph allows a tracing with signs that align with the original signing, and we examine various other properties of double covers in both signed and unsigned frameworks.

We clarify the distinct characteristics of four fundamental types of Hamiltonian dynamics: mixing, quasi-periodic, periodic, and non-hyperbolic dynamics within the framework of quantum equilibrium states. By utilizing recent research on quantum equilibrium states and analyzing the dynamics of one-body operators, we derive in-depth insights into the dynamics of these types. Specifically, our analysis determines the implications of mixing, quasi-periodic, periodic, and non-hyperbolic dynamics for systems bounded by a closed contour, as well as systems without boundary constraints. Our findings significantly contribute to understanding how Hamiltonian dynamics govern and shape quantum equilibrium states, and may have important applications in interpreting energy spectra, observing periodic orbits in quantum systems, and determining quantum thermalization rates.

We offer a straightforward pedagogical explanation of negative temperature within a two-level system, utilizing Rabi oscillations as an illustrative example. Following this, we apply this understanding to a circuit-QED setup, incorporating a two-level system and demonstrate negative temperature through both numerical simulation and experimental evidence. Finally, we explore methods for detecting negative temperature in this system.

Let's consider a finite set of integers, denoted as $A$, and an integer $k$ for which we want to explore the size of $k$-restricted signed sumsets, specifically $\{x \in \mathbb{Z} : x = \sum_{a \in A} \pm a^k\}$. We'll establish a key threshold for $|A|$ and various integers $k$ after analyzing some compelling examples and a deeper theoretical investigation. This investigation reveals that the largest possible $|A|$ is equal to $4$ when $k$ is $1$ or $2$ or any positive integer greater than $2$. We're also exploring the validity of this threshold for negative integers $k$.

A cutting-edge approach involves using deep neural networks to analyze images of colorectal adenomas for classification and severity grading. Initially, researchers focused on simplifying the process of collecting large datasets of high-quality images. They developed an efficient method for collecting more images, based on less advanced analyses, and demonstrated the potential for enhanced accuracy. A specially designed network was then tested for classification and severity grading against established standards and expert evaluations. The results showed a high potential for the network to perform these tasks with a moderate increase in depth. Additionally, a unique strategy was proposed to streamline the dataset collection process by utilizing the network's predictions. This approach was proven to yield better results than conventional methods based on shallow models. Ultimately, the study provided a foundation for similar applications involving the analysis of medical images using deep neural networks.

In addressing acoustic scattering at high frequencies, several difficulties arise, which the proposed integral equation method seeks to mitigate. This algorithm constructs a piecewise polynomial approximation of the scattering object, in combination with a non-uniform grid placement, to reduce the impact of non-coercive boundary forms and uneven surface features. Additionally, an optimized numerical solution is devised to counter the negative consequences of using the Nédélec element on non-coercive domains, especially in regards to accelerated convergence. This methodical approach is designed to enhance the rate of convergence in relation to accelerated smoothing techniques. A novel strategy is also explored to establish an approximate solution, which is demonstrated to converge at a rate of O(N-1) for specific smoothed forms, even in the presence of irregular surface features. This method is further evaluated through numerical experiments and applied to the solution of a complex acoustic scattering problem.

Two significant water-rich ancient meteorites, classified as S-type chondrites, were found in Antarctica and fell on Earth in 2018 in Benenitra, Madagascar, and Chelyabinsk, Russia. We determined the water content in five finds from Antarctica and compared it to the two fallen meteorites. It was found that the water content in the Antarctic finds ranges from 1.45 to 14.6 wt.% and averages 5.57 wt.%, which is greater than the water content in the Benenitra and Chelyabinsk fallen meteorites. The variety in water content in the Antarctic finds may be attributed to different water retention patterns in small parent bodies that survived impact and survived to reach Earth. Our research reveals a possible link between water content and the formation of chondrule rings in the Antarctic finds, with a specific trend seen in the S-type chondrite find, QUE 94206, which exhibits the highest water content among the Antarctic finds and features rare chondrule rings. We also discovered a possible link between water content and the formation of chondrule types in the Antarctic finds, with a possible link between water content and the formation of type 5 and 6 chondrules, which are rare in the Benenitra and Chelyabinsk fallen meteorites. We provide new insights into the formation of water-rich ancient meteorites and provide a new perspective on the diversity of water content in S-type chondrite finds.

This paper delves into the world of integrable higher-spin XXZ chains with both parallel and diagonal anisotropy, focusing on specific sites and their connectivity. By establishing a relationship between scalar products, form factors, and correlation functions using an algebraic approach, we gain a comprehensive understanding of the dynamics at play. In particular, we explore the structure of scalar products and form factors to uncover the underlying patterns and properties of the chain's behavior. Our detailed analysis provides a thorough explanation of the spin-spin correlation functions, revealing the interplay between anisotropy and chain connectivity on the correlation structure. Furthermore, we find that the symmetry of the chain imposes specific constraints on the correlation functions, resulting in their alignment across certain angles. This alignment gives rise to periodic fluctuations in correlations at certain anisotropy values, leading to the emergence of long-range order under specific conditions.

This study presents innovative techniques for zero-shot speech translation that significantly improve performance in few-shot settings from previously reported results. The proposed approaches build upon the Multi-Frozen Framework, a versatile framework for zero-shot speech translation utilizing shared sub-networks and sub-task specific modules. The experimental findings show that the proposed methods achieve better performance than the baseline even in the absence of data for certain source languages, and the proposed architecture's flexibility allows for easy integration with other zero-shot speech translation frameworks. The results indicate that the proposed techniques produce more accurate translations in both zero-shot and few-shot settings, and the models trained with these methods achieve higher scores in comprehensive evaluations including BLEU scores, semantic similarity, and auxiliary tasks.

In this work, higher-order multipoles beyond spherical are used to quantify the scattering of electromagnetic radiation from macroscopic ellipsoidal objects in the far field. The research reveals that the dipolar multipoles, although fundamental, are insufficient to accurately describe electromagnetic scattering. In contrast, the quadrupolar and octupolar multipoles are found to be closely intertwined and equally essential for scattering efficiency, with both contributing around 40% to the total. The relative importance of multipoles is demonstrated to depend on the shape, size, orientation, and electromagnetic properties of the object, with the ellipsoidal standard deviation varying significantly between 27% for octupolar and 63% for quadrupolar contributions. The effective cross-sectional area is proposed as a suitable normalization for scattering multipoles and may be applied to various objects and wavelengths by determining the spectral cross-sectional area. The calculated effective cross-sectional area for scattering is found to closely follow the interplay between quadrupolar and octupolar standards, with the ratio varying between 0.5 and 2.5. The relationship between multipoles and cross-sectional area is normalized such that the mean and variance are 1 for all objects and wavelengths, providing a universal reference for analyzing scattering phenomena. The research provides a fundamental understanding of electromagnetic scattering from complex objects and may have implications for the development of new scattering standards and techniques.

Following the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, there's a correspondence between Schur functions and certain macroscopic quantities like character values at group identities. Within this correspondence, specific elements known as Schur elements correspond to shifted Schur polynomials. We establish a linear transformation that maps these Schur elements to shifted Schur polynomials. This transformation is found to be governed by a basic, universal algebraic relation similar to the Cauchy identity for Schur polynomials. Additionally, we discover a broader algebraic framework that encompasses both the Schur element and shifted Schur polynomial bases for the standard representation of the symmetric group. Within this framework, we find that the Schur element and shifted Schur polynomial bases exhibit opposite centralizing properties.

We investigate a multi-GeV dark matter scenario within a dark parity symmetric framework, incorporating a minimal dark sector that includes a complex scalar, a vector, and a axial-vector. The dark parity symmetry is shown to be maintained even when the vacuum is meta-stable. Utilizing unitarity, we establish a lower limit for the mass scale (m_* \geq 10^(-3) eV) that is robust against the properties of dark matter. The choice of m_* > 10^(-3) eV results in an extremely small, yet non-negligible, contribution to the dark matter density. Furthermore, we identify the optimal parameter conditions that minimize this density while keeping the vacuum meta-stable, thus avoiding any conflict with the observed dark matter density.

We suggest that the effective spin-orbit coupling in transition metal oxides, resulting from the interaction between electrons and lattice, incorporates effects of electron interaction and crystal field splitting. This perspective is supported by research on strontium nickelates with different nickel substitutions, where experiments reveal a strong, yet unforeseen spin-orbit activation in these materials. According to our model, the effective spin-orbit coupling should be a critical factor in the unconventional magnetic domain winding of these materials, and our findings demonstrate a marked connection between this winding and the effective spin-orbit coupling, rather than being influenced by the specific details of the materials' crystal structure.

This study introduces relative $I$-functions for toric complete intersections with smooth components, establishing a connection between them and expressing one in terms of the others. Furthermore, it discovers a fundamental relationship among these $I$-functions, unveiling a deeper structural aspect of the relative $I$-functions. Additionally, when the complete intersection is non-singular, it finds that its relative $I$-functions exhibit cyclic permutation properties.

This paper investigates the potential for generating realistic, varied images of diseases through the manipulation of latent codes in generative adversarial networks (GANs), with a focus on using these images for educational purposes. By observing the code distribution of healthy images, we discovered a surprising prevalence of extraneous modes that correspond to anatomically incorrect internal structures. These modes can be either overlooked or mistaken for legitimate code structures when using unsupervised or semi-supervised learning, yet they can be easily identified and removed when using latent space optimization in a fully supervised setting. Our research finds that incorporating healthy code sampling into the training process allows GANs to produce more realistic images of diseases, but it also leads to a loss of model generalizability. Interestingly, models that fail to sample from the healthy code space exhibit improved performance when tested with unseen code structures, suggesting that they are avoiding the complex task of generating images from both disease and healthy codes. These findings raise important concerns about the validity of using GANs to create stereotypical images of diseases based on limited medical data, particularly when these models are trained with only disease codes.

ViDaExpert is an intuitive data exploration software designed for analyzing complex datasets across multiple dimensions. By utilizing advanced techniques of interactive dimension reduction, ViDaExpert enables efficient visualization of data, even in scenarios where traditional methods fail. As such, it offers a reliable solution for analyzing datasets with many variables, such as those derived from spectroscopic measurements. Building upon the algorithm described in the 2012 paper by K. K. Böckeler et al., ViDaExpert incorporates an interactive interface for identifying clusters, examining data distribution, and comparing two datasets across multiple dimensions. Furthermore, ViDaExpert provides a range of features, including the reduction of dimensions for cluster analysis and the interactive dimension reduction of data for comparison with reference data. As a standalone application developed with the Java programming language, ViDaExpert includes a range of functionalities that go beyond those described in the 2012 paper by Böckeler et al. and allows for the loading of various dataset files, such as those generated by Agilent's MassProfiler Professional software. ViDaExpert is available as a free download for all interested researchers and can be used on any computer without necessitating any additional software beyond a Java runtime environment.

This study presents a novel approach that enables the approximation of functions of two variables using a high-order representation on a square mesh element. By combining the ideas of isoparametric elements and the monomial approximation, this approach can accurately capture the behavior of functions across the element. Several options are available for selecting the order of the representation, with choices ranging from linear to quadratic, and even higher-order options. The characteristics of each type of representation are explored in some detail. It is shown that a higher-order representation with 4 degrees of freedom per side can provide a significant reduction in the error of approximation, with an $O(N^4)$ term instead of the $O(N^2)$ associated with quadratic isoparametric elements. This is particularly relevant for applications involving nonlinear problems and material models with quadratic strains. The performance of this method is demonstrated through a set of exactness tests and a sample analysis of a specific engineering problem.
